name: Timbaland
hook: A Virginia producer whose stuttering, syncopated beats blurred hip-hop and R&B production at the end of the 1990s, for Missy Elliott, Aaliyah and Jay-Z.
blurb: Timothy Mosley was born in Norfolk, Virginia, on 10 March 1972. DeVante Swing of the R&B group Jodeci took him into his crew of young musicians, Swing Mob's 'Da Bassment', with Missy Elliott, from nearby Portsmouth, and Ginuwine, and named him Timbaland, after the Timberland boot. He and Missy Elliott made records together. His breakthrough was producing most of Aaliyah's album 'One in a Million' (1996), followed by Missy Elliott's 'Supa Dupa Fly' (1997) and the albums after it, and Jay-Z's 'Big Pimpin'' (1999). His beats stutter and skip, with drums and sounds placed in unexpected gaps instead of on the beat, and they are credited with blurring the line between hip-hop and R&B. In the 2000s he produced Justin Timberlake's 'Cry Me a River' (2002) and Nelly Furtado's 'Promiscuous', carrying the same style into mainstream pop and changing its sound.

signatureTracks.title: One in a Million (Aaliyah)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The breakthrough: an R&B ballad on a skittering, half-empty beat.

signatureTracks.title: The Rain (Supa Dupa Fly) (Missy Elliott)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Slow, hollow drums with sounds dropped into the gaps.

signatureTracks.title: Cry Me a River (Justin Timberlake)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The same approach in mainstream pop, with beatboxing and choir.
